text: . Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman today discussed opportunities to further deepen the India – Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) partnership. The Finance Minister met the President of the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, Zou Jiayi, in New Delhi. In a social media post, the Finance Ministry said discussions were held on supporting India’s infrastructure and transport connectivity priorities, enhancing local-currency financing, increasing private-sector participation and the global presence of AIIB.

. India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Bihar, East Madhya Pradesh, East Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, West Bengal and North Eastern parts of the country during the next two days. IMD said that thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds are likely to prevail over Andhra Pradesh, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Bihar, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Odisha, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim tomorrow. Meanwhile, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Kerala and Mahe are expected to experience hot and humid weather till 8th of this month.

. The government has extended the last date for submission of applications by selected meritorious students for National Means cum Merit Scholarship Scheme (NMMSS) for 2026-27 to 30th September this year. The NMMSS is implemented through the National Scholarship Portal (NSP). Following the extension, the last date for Level-1 verification at the Institute Nodal Officer is 15th October while the last date for Level-2 verification with the District Nodal Officer is 31st October.The National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme awards scholarships to meritorious students from economically weaker sections to prevent drop-out of students after elementary level that is Class eight and encourage them to complete their school education up to higher secondary level that is Class 12. The scholarship amount is 12 thousand rupees per annum per student.The Scheme provides one lakh fresh scholarships every year for Class 9 students who clear the qualifying exam for the scholarship conducted by the State and UT governments. The scholarship is continued through renewal mode from Classes 10 to 12 based on the student’s academic performance. The scheme is applicable only to students studying in State Government, Government-aided and local body schools.The eligibility parameters for availing the scholarship include parental income of not more than 3.50 lakh rupees per annum, a minimum of 55 per cent marks or equivalent grade in the Class 8 examination for appearing in the selection test for award of scholarship. The government has advised all the eligible students to complete their scholarship applications on the National Scholarship Portal within the extended timeline.

. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has said that India should pursue technological innovation at scale, but without compromising human responsibility, safety and public trust.Addressing the Global Fintech Festival 2026, the Finance Minister said India’s young generation was not waiting for opportunities but was creating platforms, enterprises and new solutions. She said India’s demographic dividend was visible in the country’s rapidly growing technology and fintech ecosystem.Smt. Sitharaman also questioned those who view India’s demographic dividend through a lens of perpetual pessimism. Referring to sceptics in a lighter vein, she said “naraz fufa jis” are never short of reasons to doubt India’s moment and capabilities.Highlighting the challenges posed by emerging technologies, the Finance Minister described Artificial Intelligence as a double-edged sword. She said AI can help detect fraud faster, but can also enable perpetrators to automate larger and more sophisticated frauds.Finance Minister stressed the need for greater institutional accountability in the development and deployment of Artificial Intelligence. She said speed and efficiency should not come at the cost of safety, transparency and human oversight. Regulators, boards and senior management, she said, must understand how AI is used, the decisions it influences and the risks involved.She also called for stronger cybersecurity, data protection, consumer protection and cooperation between regulators and innovators. The Finance Minister said the success of India’s fintech sector should be measured not only by transactions and valuations, but also by the trust it earns and the problems it solves.Smt. Sitharaman also urged the Reserve Bank of India to further advance its wholesale and retail Central Bank Digital Currency pilots, citing the growing momentum in tokenisation and digital finance.

. The Meeting planned on Monday between Iran and the Gulf countries to discuss arrangements for shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, has been postponed. Oman’s Foreign Minister Badr bin Hamad Al Busaidi announced the development late Sunday evening. He said the regional meeting scheduled for Monday in Salalah has been postponed ‘in the interest of consensus’, while stressing Oman’s continued commitment to dialogue, regional stability and long-term cooperation.Iranian state-affiliated media reported that the meeting was postponed at the request of some regional countries and that the decision was made jointly by Iran and Oman. Iran had earlier said that it had reached an understanding with Oman on a new maritime route through the strait.The postponement of the Iran-Gulf meeting is a setback for diplomacy at a time when pressure on both major regional shipping routes – through the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea, is increasing. Global Oil prices recorded another jump on Monday, with Brent Crude futures trading over 107 USD a barrel and WTI at over 102 USD.

. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has congratulated Prime Minister Narendra Modi for the success of BRICS Summit 2026 in New Delhi, saying that its success left an indelible mark on the global stage. He said that the signing of the landmark New Delhi Declaration is not just a document but is a statement of India’s growing global influence under the leadership of Prime Minister Modi. The historic BRICS Summit has successfully concluded in New Delhi yesterday.In a social media post, the Minister said that under the visionary leadership of Mr Modi, India underlined Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability as its foremost priorities as BRICS Chair. He said, guided by these priorities, India has laid special emphasis on connecting BRICS cooperation directly with the common people.The Minister said this inclusive and human-centric approach became the hallmark of BRICS Summit in New Delhi. He highlighted that India has put the Global South at the centre, not at the margins, championing a more inclusive, representative and balanced world order. Rooted in country’s civilisational ethos of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam, India has once again shown that leadership is not about having the loudest voice but the strongest consensus.

. On the eve of Raksha Bandhan, President Droupadi Murmu has extended greetings to people. The President said that the festival of Raksha Bandhan has been an integral part of country’s culture and tradition since ancient times. She said that rakhi thread, tied around the wrist with faith, is regarded as a sacred bond of protection, known as Raksha Bandhan.The President  said that in many shlokas and mantras, Rakshe, Ma Chala, Ma Chala can be found which expresses the imploration that may this bond of protection continue forever. President Murmu urged every citizen to take a pledge to strengthen the bonds amongst families and communities, marching forward with this spirit towards a Viksit Bharat.Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla also extended greetings to countrymen on the eve of Raksha Bandhan. In his message, Mr Birla said festival that celebrates the mutual love, affection, and trust between brothers and sisters. He noted that the festival symbolizes of India’s rich culture, family values, and the unbreakable bonds of affection and belonging.

. The Archaeological Survey of India has notified Gollala Gudi Temple at Palampet in the Mulugu district of Telangana as a monument of national importance. The Ministry of culture said that the temple is situated near the UNESCO listed Ramappa Temple and is renowned for its exquisite carvings and architectural heritage.The temple is a Trikutalaya and consists of a mandapa facing East and surrounded by three garbhagriha.A monument of national importance in the country is protected under the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958. The Archaeological Survey of India takes charge of such sites for conservation, maintenance, and regulated public access

. Iran and Oman have agreed on new entry and exit shipping routes for the Strait of Hormuz, which they plan to present to other Gulf nations at an upcoming regional meeting.Under this new plan, the entry route into the Gulf will sit entirely within Iranian territorial waters, and a section of the exit route will also fall under Iranian control. Once this new system starts operating, the waterway’s southern route will be closed, directly opposing the United States’ demands to keep it open.Furthermore, Iranian officials emphasised that this agreement does not mean the Strait of Hormuz is being reopened. Iran has set seven conditions for the U.S. before the waterway can open, and it will remain closed until those demands are met.Iran’s Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei announced on Friday that Gulf littoral states’ foreign ministers are scheduled to meet in Oman tomorrow to exchange views on regional issues, including the Iran-Oman talks on designating safe routes in the Strait of Hormuz.

. In the Women’s T20 Asia Cup cricket final, India will face defending champions Sri Lanka in Dubai today. The match will begin at 8 PM Indian time. Both India and Sri Lanka have reached the final unbeaten.Seven-time champions India have reached the final topping Group A with three wins before defeating Bangladesh by 40 runs in the semi-final.Sri Lanka also remained unbeaten in the group stage, winning all three matches before overcoming Pakistan by four wickets in the semi-final. India are the most successful team in Women’s Asia Cup history with seven titles.

. England moved a little closer to India in the World Test Championship (WTC) points table after beating Pakistan in the third Test at Edgbaston, Birmingham. Pakistan have lost further ground in the WTC standings, being already at the dead bottom ahead of the Birmingham loss. England have consolidated their sixth spot in the nine-team standings.Australia continue to hold the top spot in the WTC standings. South Africa occupy the second spot, followed by New Zealand. Bangladesh are ahead of India and occupy the fourth spot. Sri Lanka and West Indies are seventh and eighth, respectively, in the points table. The top two will secure the places for the WTC final from June 9 to 13.

. The Quad partners-India, Australia, Japan and the United States conducted a tabletop exercise in Tokyo on the 3rd and 4th of this month to advance the Quad Indo-Pacific Logistics Network (IPLN) and enhance civilian response efforts across the region. The exercise was hosted by Japan’s Ministry of Defense.The Ministry of External Affairs said, the exercise focused on natural disaster response scenarios, through which the Quad partners examined ways to leverage each other’s logistics capabilities. The exercise also aimed to strengthen interoperability and streamline coordination among the four partners.The Ministry said, the exercise marked significant progress towards developing Standard Operating Procedures for the IPLN, which will provide an institutional framework for its effective operationalisation.The Quad partners expressed their deepest condolences to all those affected by the recent devastating floods and reaffirmed their shared commitment to supporting regional partners in times of need. They also discussed ways to coordinate humanitarian assistance and disaster relief efforts during crises and emergencies.The tabletop exercise reaffirmed the Quad’s commitment to strengthening practical cooperation to address regional challenges and ensure a free and open Indo-Pacific. The partners will continue efforts to operationalise the IPLN through tabletop and field training exercises, confidence-building measures and exchanges among subject-matter experts.

. Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Governor Sanjay Malhotra has said that inflows through the Foreign Currency Non-Resident (Bank) [FCNR-B] and the other schemes have been ‘very robust’. In an interview with a private television channel, the RBI Governor said the strong inflows reflect confidence in India’s macroeconomic fundamentals and demonstrate the ability to attract foreign capital within a short period.On the surplus liquidity in the banking system, Malhotra said the Reserve Bank has enough tools at its disposal to manage liquidity and is prepared to use them as needed. He added that some of the surplus liquidity would be withdrawn over time through currency circulation, forex intervention and banks’ reserve requirements amid rising credit growth. Malhotra added that the central ​bank’s objective was to maintain appropriate liquidity conditions and keep the weighted average call rate aligned with the repo rate.The RBI Governor said the Monetary Policy Committee would reassess growth and inflation dynamics at its meeting next month amid rising prices of crude oil owing to the ongoing West Asia crisis. Sanjay Malhotra noted that the impact of higher crude prices on inflation would depend on the extent to which the increase is passed through to consumers.He said the government has to a great degree, absorbed and cushioned the shock; as a result, the Indian economy has weathered it well. On stronger-than-expected growth in the April to June quarter, the RBI Governor said it was not entirely surprising. He added that incoming corporate data was also pointing to firmer growth. The central bank saw no signs of overheating, including in consumption loans.

. The Leaders’ Session of BRICS Business Forum is underway at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi.  Heads of State of BRICS Member Countries including Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Russian President Vladimir Putin, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and South African President Cyril Ramaphosa are attending the session.In his address, Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal said that during India’s Chairship, BRICS has been driven by a clear purpose, to achieve more balanced trade amongst member nations and to explore expansion of trade in services across the bloc.He said exports from BRICS countries have risen from about USD 900 billion in 2003 to USD 6 trillion in 2024, reflecting the scale of its market and potential.He said, under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, India remains committed to ensure that this cooperation reaches those who form the backbone of the BRICS economies . Mr Goyal said, it must benefit the farmers, empower women in business and beyond and provide greater opportunities for wealth and prosperity to young entrepreneurs and MSMEs. He said, with the participation over two thousand business leaders and delegates from member countries and partner countries, this is the largest BRICS Business Forum ever held. He mentioned that the Forum has taken up issues such as non-tariff barriers, impacting global value chains, agriculture and agri-technology, services trade, women-led enterprises and the digital economy.

. In Asian markets today, South Korea’s Kospi fell nearly 1.8 per cent, while Japan’s Nikkei 225 dropped over 1.9 per cent.In European markets, London’s FTSE 100 rose 0.6 per cent, while Germany’s DAX was trading 0.7 per cent up, when reports last came in. On economic front, United Kingdom’s real gross domestic product grew by 0.4 per cent in July, following a 0.3 per cent expansion in June, according to the figures released today by the Office for National Statistics.

. Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla has extended his wishes to the citizens on the occasion of Hindi Diwas today. In a social media post, Mr Birla said that from literature and journalism to cinema, television, education, and the digital world, Hindi has become a powerful medium of expression for millions of people. He said that in the age of the internet, social media, digital education, technology, and artificial intelligence, the role of Indian languages is becoming increasingly vital.The Lok Sabha Speaker emphasised that Hindi is emerging as an effective language for knowledge, science, technology, and modern expression. He further said that Hindi has given identity to India’s confidence, pride, and global stature and it is the responsibility of the citizens to connect Hindi with the new generation, new technologies, and new opportunities.Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has extended his greetings to the countrymen on the occasion of Hindi Diwas today. In a social media post, Mr Singh said that Hindi is not merely a language, but a powerful expression of India’s culture, civilization, and life values. The Defence Minister added that Hindi is the language that weaves India’s diversity into the thread of unity. He also urged the citizens to resolve to preserve and promote the Hindi language, and make it even more robust in the fields of knowledge, science, technology, and innovation.

. India has set the Guinness World Record with World’s Longest Steel Slag Road at Raigarh in Chhattisgarh. The 1.85-kilometre road marks a major scale-up of an indigenous technology that converts processed steel slag, a by-product of steel production, into aggregates for road construction.Speaking at the conferment ceremony of the Guinness World Record in New Delhi today, Science and Technology Minister Dr Jitendra Singh said that Steel Slag Road Technology can reduce road construction costs by around 40 per cent while delivering four times the strength of conventional roads. He said that this technology is being pursued by CSIR-Central Road Research Institute (CSIR-CRRI) New Delhi with private sector participation.Dr Singh said that this initiative simultaneously lives up to more than one flagship priorities of this government emphasising on Waste to Wealth recycling options. He said that the technology can also substantially extend the maintenance cycle, with a re-look required only after about 15 years in suitable applications, making it a breakthrough with implications not only for road engineering but also for the overall infrastructure economy.The Minister called for the indigenous technology to move from one project to many projects and from one State to many States, with its adoption extending beyond the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways to Railways, other Government departments, State Governments and private builders.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has expressed gratitude to the leaders of all the BRICS member countries for making the Delhi summit of the grouping productive and outcome-oriented. A video reflecting key moments of the two-day summit was posted on the social media handles of the prime minister. In the video, a part of the prime minister’s summit speech was shown where he said through BRICS, India has advanced friendship, partnership and cooperation all across.The leaders who attended the summit included Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Abu Dhabi’s Crown Prince Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan. Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, Vietnamese Prime Minister Le Minh Hung, Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto, Egypt’s President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, President of the Philippines Ferdinand R Marcos Jr, Uganda’s Vice President Jessica Alupo, besides others, also attended the summit.India hosted the BRICS Summit on September 12-13 and it was attended by the leaders of the 11 member countries and 10 partner countries of the grouping, besides some international organisations. Mr Modi also held 15 sit-down bilateral meetings with heads of states or heads of governments in the last three days on the sidelines of the summit.

. The 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit in Bishkek has concluded with 13 key outcomes. The outcomes cover counter-terrorism, climate action, energy, disaster management and digital cooperation.The summit adopted the historic Bishkek Declaration, marking the SCO’s 25th anniversary. It also approved four MoUs and more than 20 decisions.A major decision was to include English as an official SCO language. Leaders also agreed to establish a Universal Centre for Countering Security Threats.The measures will strengthen cooperation against terrorism, extremism, organised crime and other transnational threats. They will also improve security information sharing.Several decisions focus on tackling drug trafficking and synthetic drugs. These include stronger coordination among law enforcement agencies and a cooperation programme on combating drug addiction until 2030. The measures support India’s efforts against cross-border narcotics trafficking and narco-terrorism.On climate and energy, SCO members agreed to enhance cooperation on energy conservation and efficiency. They also adopted a memorandum on combating climate change. These measures support India’s energy security and climate-resilient development goals.The summit also adopted a statement on assistance to countries affected by emergencies. It will strengthen cooperation in disaster management and humanitarian assistance, an area where India has significant capabilities.In the digital sector, members agreed to expand cooperation in artificial intelligence. The move will provide India an opportunity to share its digital and AI expertise and promote responsible and inclusive use of the technology.An agreement on information cooperation will also promote institutional exchanges and help strengthen India’s engagement with the regional media space.The Ministry of External Affairs said the outcomes give India a strategic platform to advance its positions on regional security, development and connectivity. They also strengthen India’s engagement with Central Asia and the wider Eurasian region.The MEA said, addressing the summit, Prime Minister Narendra Modi called for a roadmap for the next 25 years. He stressed the need for concrete outcomes in the areas of security, connectivity and opportunity.The two-day SCO Summit was held at Bishkek in Kyrgyzstan, from August 31 to September 1.

The Ministry of Education, in coordination with the External Affairs Ministry is organizing a two day Bharat Innovates Exposition from today at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi to showcase India’s Deep-Tech innovations as a lead up to and alongside the 18th BRICS Summit 2026. The Exposition is showcasing 37 India’s Deep-Tech startups and ventures alligning with the theme of India’s BRICS Chairship Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability. The event is providing participating innovators an opportunity to network with CEOs, investors, business leaders and industry representatives from BRICS member countries. Ministry of Eduaction said that the event will facilitate opportunities for Business to Business engagements, technology partnerships, investment discussions, business linkages and international market access.

. Union Home Minister Amit Shah announced that Bharatiya Janata Party workers, NDA partners and several voluntary organisations will undertake the “Seva Sankalp Abhiyan” across the country between 17th of this month and 17th of October.Addressing media persons in Mumbai, Mr. Shah said, the campaign aims to contribute to the vision of a Viksit Bharat through Jan Bhagidari. Mr. Shah said, 17th of September marks Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s birthday, while October this year marks the completion of 25 years of his public service as Chief Minister and Prime Minister. He also highlighted various infrastructure, social and cultural initiatives undertaken under the NDA government led by Prime Minister Modi.

. Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla has extended his greetings to the citizens on the occasion of Hartalika Teej today. In a social media post, Mr Birla said that the festival symbolises good fortune and unbreakable marital love. He added that the festival is associated with Goddess Parvati’s unwavering penance, resolve, and the worship of Lord Shiva.The Lok Sabha Speaker emphasised that amidst nature adorned with greenery, the festival of Teej conveys the message of remaining sensitive to nature alongside the cultural traditions. He also wished that the grace of Goddess Gauri and Lord Shiva bring good fortune, happiness, peace, and prosperity into everyone’s lives, and that the earth remains lush green, healthy, and prosperous forever.
. In the Indian bullion market today, 24 carat gold was 0.9 per cent down at 1,51,938 rupees per 10 grams. Silver also dropped two per cent to 2,28,920 rupees per kilogram.

. Top-ranked India’s Dhiraj Bommadevara scripted history by becoming the first Indian male recurve archer to win gold at the World Cup Final, edging Japan’s Nakanishi Junya in a thrilling shoot-off at Saltillo in Mexico.The 25-year-old World Number 10 Army man produced a dominant run, powering through the quarterfinals and semifinals before overcoming world No. 20 Nakanishi 6-5 in a hard-fought five-setter. After a 5-5 tie, Dhiraj prevailed 10-9 in the shoot-off. He also ended a 16-year wait for an Indian male recurve archer to win a medal in this prestigious event. Jayanta Talukdar was the last male recurve archer to win a medal – a bronze in Edinburgh 2010.Dola Banerjee remains the only other Indian to have won World Cup Final gold, claiming the women’s individual title in the 2007 edition in Dubai.

. Markets regulator SEBI on Saturday proposed changes to the methodology for calculating expiry-day settlement prices of index and stock derivatives, following a review of the newly introduced closing auction session (CAS) framework.In a consultation paper, SEBI proposed two options for determining the settlement prices, a blended Volume Weighted Average Price – VWAP based on trades executed during the last 30 minutes of the continuous trading session – CTS, and the 10-minute CAS, or continuation of the existing CTS VWAP methodology. The proposals follow feedback received from market participants on the use of the CAS-determined closing price for settling derivative contracts on expiry. Determination of derivative settlement prices based on the closing price arrived at through CAS was among the significant areas of feedback received by SEBI.SEBI introduced the CAS framework in the equity cash segment from August 3 to determine the closing price of securities. Under the current framework, the closing price determined through CAS also serves as the basis for determining settlement prices of derivative contracts on expiry. The use of the CAS-determined closing price for expiry-day settlement of derivatives has been one of the key concerns raised by market participants, prompting Sebi to review the existing methodology.On 3rd September, SEBI had said it may propose changes to the methodology following the feedback and indicated that a consultation paper on the proposed framework was likely to be released in about a week. The proposed changes are aimed at addressing concerns around the use of the CAS-determined closing price as the basis for settling derivative contracts on expiry. The Securities and Exchange Board of India – SEBI has sought comments from stakeholders on the proposals till 3rd October.

. In Indonesia, the death toll has risen to six after a ferry carrying more than 240 people overturned due to bad weather in the Java Sea today.Nearly 130 passengers and crew members remain missing. Indonesian rescuers said, at least 107 people have been rescued so far, as search and rescue operations continue around the vessel’s last known location. The ferry was travelling from East Java to South Kalimantan and had departed from Surabaya for Banjarmasin on Borneo Island. Ferries are a common mode of transport in Indonesia, an archipelago of more than 17,000 islands.

. In tennis, India’s SD Prajwal Dev, partnering France’s Constantin Bittoun Kouzmine, has won his second ATP Challenger doubles title at the Sport Festival Challenger in Phan Thiet, Vietnam.The top-seeded Indo-French duo defeated Japan’s Yamato Sueoka and Naoki Tajima 6-1, 7-6 in the final yesterday. This is Dev’s second ATP Challenger Tour doubles title. His maiden title came in 2023 at the President’s Cup in Kazakhstan, where he partnered fellow Indian Niki Kaliyanda Poonacha.The Challenger 50 event, played on hard courts, began on the 7th of this month and concludes today.

. Science and Technology Minister Dr Jitendra Singh has said that critical minerals are key to India’s energy security, industrial competitiveness and national security. The Minister said this while addressing a special plenary of the 3rd Global Summit on Advanced Materials, Critical Minerals, and Metals in New Delhi. Dr Singh said that critical minerals and metals will be a driving component of the next phase of technological development, with their importance extending beyond mining to energy security, industrial competitiveness and national security. He said that the global economy is undergoing a paradigm shift, with clean energy, electric mobility, semiconductors, telecommunications, aerospace, defence and nuclear energy emerging as major drivers of technological and industrial transformation. He added, India is now participating in this global discourse with much greater confidence and is preparing to assume a larger global role.Dr. Singh has called for early industry linkage with research and innovation, saying potential industry partners should be brought on board right from the beginning. He further said that a healthy synergy among research, industry, government and the non-government sector is essential for sustaining startups and entrepreneurs. The Minister also highlighted on building domestic capabilities for energy security as the world moves towards cleaner and greener sources of energy. He said that India’s next phase of growth in strategic technologies and materials will depend on working together of all stakeholders.

. Hindi Diwas is being celebrated across the country today. It was on this day in 1949 that the Constituent Assembly adopted Hindi written in Devanagari script as the official language of the country. Today, Hindi is one of the widely spoken languages in the world and the first language of more than 52 crore people.Union Home Minister Amit Shah will attend the Hindi Diwas 2026 program and the 6th All India Rajbhasha Sammelan (Official Language Conference) in Navi Mumbai today.The two-day All India Official Language Conference is being organised in Navi Mumbai, Maharashtra, by the Department of Official Language under the Ministry of Home Affairs. The conference aims to highlight the relationship between Hindi and Maharashtra’s rich linguistic, cultural and literary traditions. In the inaugural session today, Union Home Minister Amit Shah will present the ‘Rajbhasha Gaurav’ and ‘Rajbhasha Kirti’ Awards for 2025-26.Several important books and publications will also be launched. An exhibition featuring stalls by various institutions, organisations, banks and ministries is also being organised. A key attraction of this year’s conference will be a discussion centred on the National Song ‘Vande Mataram’.Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, Deputy Chief Ministers Eknath Shinde and Sunetra Pawar, several Members of Parliament, scholars, litterateurs, educationists and senior officials will attend the conference.

. Bangladesh has reported 1,022 deaths linked to confirmed measles and suspected measles cases since March 15, while dengue has claimed 149 lives so far this year. According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), seven children died with suspected measles symptoms, while 905 new suspected measles cases and 63 confirmed cases in the last 24 hours.Meanwhile, six people died and 1,561 were hospitalised with dengue in the last 24 hours.

. Union Home Minister Amit Shah has said that BJP-led NDA governments in 21 states will introduce Uniform Civil Code (UCC) before 2029. Speaking to reporters in Mumbai, Home Minister said, UCC has been introduced in several states and he is confident that it will be introduced in the 21 BJP-NDA ruled states before 2029. Mr Shah said, triple talaq has been abolished, giving Muslim women equal rights. He said the government has strengthened the country’s criminal justice system through the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and claimed that several states have recorded a 30 per cent increase in the conviction rate in a single year. Home Minister also said a system is being established to ensure justice ccan be delivered within three years.On national security, Mr Shah said the abrogation of Articles 370 and 35A had been achieved without a single drop of blood being shed or a bullet being fired, and asserted that Kashmir is now fully integrated with India. He said the government has ended five decades of Naxalism and signed more than 14 peace agreements in the country’s North-East region. Mr Shah said, surgical strikes, air strikes and Operation Sindoor have established a policy of zero tolerance towards terrorism.

. President Droupadi Murmu has extended greetings on the occasion of Ganesh Chaturthi. In her message, the President said that Lord  Ganesha symbolises wisdom, prosperity and auspicious beginnings. The festival of Ganesh Chaturthi brings energy, knowledge and positivity into our lives. She said that the sacred festival inspires everyone to move forward on the path of progress with new resolutions in life. President Murmu prayed that Lord Ganesha brings happiness, peace, good health and prosperity into everyone’s lives.Prime Minister Narnedra modi has extended his greetings to the citizens on the occasion of Ganesh Chaturthi today. Sharing Sanskrit Subhashitam in a social media post, Mr Modi wished that the sacred festival infuses new energy and fresh enthusiasm into everyone’s lives. He also wished that all endeavours succeed through the divine blessings of Lord Ganesha, and the nation continues to advance on the path of constant progress.

. In Hockey, India’s men’s and women’s teams have clinched the Junior Asia Cup titles at Moqi in China today. The Indian Men’s team defeated South Korea four-one in the final to successfully defend its title. Ajeet Yadav, Anmol Ekka, Prabhdeep Singh and Ashu Maurya scored for India. With this victory, India became the first team in the history of the tournament to win the Men’s title four times, following earlier triumphs in 2015, 2023 and 2024.The Indian women’s team also emerged victorious, defeating hosts China one-nil in the final. Sanika Chandrakant Mane scored the only goal in the 17th minute to secure the title for India. The victory completed a hat-trick of Junior Asia Cup titles for the Indian women’s team, which had previously won in 2023 and 2024.Both the Indian men’s and women’s teams have also qualified for the Junior Hockey World Cup by winning their respective Asia Cup titles.Prime Minister Narendra Modi has congratulated India’s Junior Women’s Hockey Team on retaining the Asia Cup title with an unbeaten campaign. In a social media post, Mr. Modi said the team’s success reflects the talent and determination of the players and extended his best wishes to the entire team.The Prime Minister also congratulated the Junior Men’s Hockey Team on winning the Asia Cup with an emphatic 4-1 victory over South Korea in the final. Describing the achievement as remarkable, Mr. Modi said it reflects the immense talent of the young players.Home Minister Amit Shah has congratulated junior women’s hockey team on winning the Asia Cup and bringing pride and joy to the entire nation. Sharing a social media post, Mr Shah said that their victory and dominant display of sporting prowess will inspire more budding players to join the list of India’s champions. Mr Shah also congratulated Indian junior men’s hockey team for winning the Asia Cup. He added that with the vigour and command of the game, they have once again demonstrated that true mettle of Indian sportsmanship and set an inspiring example for others to follow.

. The Archery Premier League (APL) is set for a bigger second season, with 36 of India’s leading archers set to compete alongside 12 international stars from 10 countries in Hyderabad from October 8 to 18. The expanded field brings together Olympic medallists, world champions, World Cup winners and some of the biggest names in the sport, adding further international flavour to the six-franchise competition.Four-time Olympian Deepika Kumari and World Championship silver medallist Atanu Das headline India’s recurve contingent, with reigning Asian champion Dhiraj Bommadevara also part of the field. The compound section features multi-time World Cup and Asian Games champion Jyothi Surekha Vennam, former World No. 1 Abhishek Verma and former World Champion Ojas Pravin Deotale.The international contingent is led by Tokyo 2020 Olympic champion Mete Gazoz of Türkiye, Paris 2024 bronze medallist Casey Kaufhold of the United States, Brazil’s World No. 1 Marcus D’Almeida and Great Britain’s World No. 2 Ella Gibson. Dutch compound star Mike Schloesser, a former World Champion and four-time World Cup Final winner, will also compete.The league will also feature all 12 members of India’s Asian Games-bound archery squad, giving the APL added relevance ahead of the country’s campaign in Aichi-Nagoya later this month. Among those entering the league for the first time are World Championships silver medallist Rajat Chauhan, World Cup stage gold medallist Ridhi, World University Games gold medallist Kushal Dalal and junior national champion Kirti Sharma.The second season will retain one of the league’s most distinctive features – its 15-second shot clock. Five seconds quicker than the standard Olympic timing, the format is designed to place greater emphasis on speed, decision-making and composure under pressure. Initiated by the Archery Association of India with the support of the Government of Telangana, the league will feature six mixed-gender franchise teams competing across the Recurve and Compound categories. The 11-day tournament will be held at People’s Plaza on Hyderabad’s Necklace Road. Rajputana Royals won the inaugural edition, which also generated significant digital engagement among younger audiences.

. India produced a commanding all-round performance to defeat Sri Lanka by 72 runs in the Women’s Asia Cup 2026 final in Dubai last night, securing a record-extending eighth Asia Cup title. The victory also helped India avenge their defeat to Sri Lanka in the 2024 final. It was India’s sixth win over Sri Lanka in an Asia Cup final across the ODI and T20 formats, including the 2004 edition when India defeated Sri Lanka 5-0 in the two-team tournament.India first posted a formidable 183 for 5 after openers Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana produced a record-breaking 129-run partnership. The bowlers then completed the job by dismissing Sri Lanka for 111 in 19.4 overs, with Shree Charani taking four wickets and Deepti Sharma claiming three. Shafali Verma was declared Player of the Match.India’s victory was built on a combination of explosive batting at the top and disciplined bowling through the middle and final overs. The record partnership between Shafali and Mandhana gave India the platform, while Charani and Deepti dismantled Sri Lanka’s chase to seal a memorable eighth title.President Droupadi Murmu, Vice President C P Radhakrishnan and Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulated all the members of Team India on winning Women’s T20 Asia Cup Championship 2026. In a social media post, the President said that the players played superbly as a team throughout the tournament, winning all the matches and making the country proud. She said that these players are a source of great inspiration for the youth of the country. She also expressed confidence that the team will script many more inspiring chapters of success and excellence.Vice President C P Radhakrishnan also congratulated the team on lifting the Women’s T20 Asia Cup for a record eighth time. He said that the team’s unbeaten campaign, exceptional teamwork and unwavering determination throughout the tournament have brought immense pride to the nation. He also wished the players well for their future endeavours.Prime Minister Modi said that the confidence, consistency and remarkable spirit of the players were on full display throughout the tournament. Congratulating the Women’s team, Mr Modi wished that this triumph inspire millions of youngsters across the country to play more and shine.

. Today is World Suicide Prevention Day. The day is observed worldwide to raise awareness about suicide prevention and the importance of mental health.The occasion reminds us that people facing emotional distress or difficult circumstances need timely support, understanding and appropriate care. Experts emphasise that listening to someone with patience and without judgement can encourage them to seek help and support.On this Day, people are encouraged to remain attentive to the emotional well-being of those around them and, when required, guide them towards family members, trusted persons or mental health professionals.

. Diplomatic efforts are back in focus this week as the US-Iran conflict continues to disrupt the Gulf and widen to other areas. Iran and the Gulf states are due to meet in Oman on Monday to discuss the Strait of Hormuz and the broader regional security. Iran says it has reached an understanding with Oman on a new maritime route through the strait. However, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has said that this does not mean an immediate reopening of Hormuz, which will depend on conditions being met by the United States. Further, it remains to be seen if all the Gulf Countries will be present for this meeting – Bahrain has said earlier that it will not participate.Meanwhile, maritime security in the Strait of Hormuz continues to remain a major concern. The UK Maritime Trade Operations agency reported on Sunday that a projectile hit a vessel while it was transiting the Strait of Hormuz. The extent of the damage and the condition of the crew were not immediately known. Separately, Iranian state media reported that an Iranian commercial vessel was struck near Qeshm Island, killing one person and injuring three others.In Saudi Arabia, the Houthis have claimed another attack using missiles and drones against a military base in the south. Saudi civil defense overnight said a projectile fell in al-Tawwal governorate near the border with Yemen along the Red Sea, injuring two people and damaging a mosque and several other buildings. The statement blamed the Houthis. It also said sirens went off in Sharurah province but didn’t report casualties or damage.In Iraq, authorities have seized a drone-launching platform linked to the attack on Saudi Arabia’s East-West oil pipeline and are continuing their investigation. Iraq had earlier closed several crossings with Iran as part of the security operation and it has been now Iraqi authorities have reportedly announced a timeline to reopen some of these crossings.The wider concern is that the conflict is now putting pressure on both major maritime routes, i.e. the Strait of Hormuz and Bab-el-Mandeb, with the eyes on what happens in Monday’s diplomatic meeting in Oman.

. In Indonesia, around 140 passengers and crew are missing after a ferry carrying more than 240 people overturned in bad weather in the Java Sea today.Indonesian rescuers said at least 102 people have been rescued and the body of one passenger has been recovered as search operations continue around the vessel’s last known position.The ferry was travelling from East Java to South Kalimantan province. It had departed from Surabaya, Indonesia’s second-largest city, for Banjarmasin on Borneo Island. Indonesia is an archipelago of more than 17,000 islands, where ferries are a common mode of transport.Last month, at least 211 people were rescued after an Indonesian ferry caught fire in rough seas near the tourist island of Bali. One person died, and four others remained missing.Today’s accident comes four days after a passenger ferry fire in the Philippines killed at least 76 people, with more than 10 others still missing.

. The Associated Chambers of Commerce and Industry of India (ASSOCHAM) has hailed Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision for strengthening BRICS as a powerful platform for global cooperation and a stronger voice for the Global South. President of ASSOCHAM Nirmal K Minda said that the Prime Minister’s vision of transforming BRICS cooperation into concrete business outcomes is highly significant. He added that deepening trade, investment, technology, start-up and business partnerships among BRICS economies can unlock enormous opportunities and create new avenues for inclusive and sustainable growth.Mr Minda said that the emphasis on innovation, digital solutions, infrastructure, strategic technologies and initiatives such as the BRICS Startup Innovation Fund can further strengthen collaboration and enable Indian enterprises to scale globally.

. In men’s cricket, India will begin their three-match T20 International series against Afghanistan at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in Delhi this evening. The match will start at 7 PM Indian time. The remaining two matches of the series will be played at the same venue on Tuesday and Thursday.Shreyas Iyer will lead India, with Tilak Varma as his deputy. Teenage batter Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has also been named in the team.India have won eight of their nine T20Is against Afghanistan, with one match ending without a result.Meanwhile, Delhi Traffic Police has issued an advisory for spectators, as the match coincides with the second and final day of the BRICS Summit. Traffic restrictions, diversions and parking regulations will be in place in and around the stadium and parts of central Delhi from 2 PM onwards.Spectators have been advised to plan their journeys, use alternate routes and use only designated entry, parking and app-based taxi pick-up and drop-off points.

. The festival of Ganesh Chaturthi is being celebrated today across the country with great devotion. The day marks the birth of Lord Ganesha, who is a symbol of wisdom, prosperity and good fortune. Also known as Vinayaka Chaturthi or Ganesh Utsav, the day marks the beginning of ten-day-long festivities during which people place clay idols of Lord Ganesha at their homes and worship them.The festivities conclude with the grand event of Ganesh Visarjan, where the idols of Lord Ganesha are immersed in water bodies, symbolising the cycle of creation and dissolution. The idols are carried in grand processions from homes and pandals to rivers, lakes, or seas, accompanied by chants of “Ganapati Bappa Morya,” bhajans, and dances.Ganesh Chaturthi is a major attraction in Maharashtra, where people celebrate it with great zeal.

. India’s 2026 BRICS Presidency is broadening historically strong oil-related ties with the Gulf into a wider partnership spanning investment, technology, food security, clean energy and regional stability, a report has said.The report published in a daily published from UAE said energy ties remain the foundation of the relationship at the 18th BRICS Summit, but cooperation is expanding into new strategic areas. During Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit to the UAE this year, both the countries deepened collaboration on crude oil, LNG and LPG, and agreed to increase UAE participation in India’s strategic petroleum reserves and explored strategic gas reserves.Another area of co-operation is food-security which can link Gulf demand with India’s agricultural and food-processing capabilities. Investment in storage, logistics and reliable supply chains can be explored, the report noted. Highlighting the timing of the event, the report said that regional tensions have renewed attention on energy security, maritime trade and safe shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, while Gulf states diversify their economies, invest in advanced technology and strengthen commercial links with Asia.The Gulf is represented in the expanded BRICS through Saudi Arabia and the UAE, providing the bloc greater weight in the global energy and finance landscape. India-Gulf ties grew stronger in February this year, when the country signed terms of reference with GCC and formally launched negotiations for a comprehensive free trade agreement, covering Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the UAE.

. The Government has announced the Tenzing Norgay National Adventure Awards for the year 2024. The awards recognise outstanding achievements by individuals in the field of adventure and seek to promote a spirit of endurance, risk-taking, teamwork and quick and effective decision-making in challenging situations. The awards are given in four categories, which are Land Adventure, Water Adventure, Air Adventure and Lifetime Achievement. Each awardee will receive a statuette, a certificate and award money of 15 lakh rupees. The awardees are Baljeet Kaur and Skalzang Rigzin in Land Adventure category, Rimo Saha in Water Adventure category and Shiv Prasad Chamoli in the Life Time Achievement category.The selections were made following the recommendations of the National Selection Committee. The Committee evaluated the nominations and recommended the awardees for conferment of the national honour.The awards seek to promote among the youth a spirit of courage, endurance, discipline, risk-taking and cooperative teamwork, while encouraging the ability to respond with speed and effectiveness in challenging situations. President Droupadi Murmu will confer the awards along with the National Sports Awards 2025. The date of the award ceremony will be announced later.

. Vultures are extremely important for our ecosystem. By feeding on dead animals, they help keep the environment clean and reduce the spread of harmful diseases.However, vulture populations have declined significantly because of habitat loss, poisoning, and certain veterinary medicines that are harmful to them. Conservation efforts are therefore essential to protect these birds and maintain the balance of nature.On this International Vulture Day, government and environmental experts have urged people to understand, protect, and conserve vultures for a healthier environment.

. Iraq has dismissed the commander of military operations in Maysan province and reportedly ordered a temporary closure of the Shalamcheh border crossing with Iran as a precaution, following an investigation into the drone attacks on Saudi Arabia’s East-West Pipeline.Saudi Arabia had earlier stated that the attacks originated from Iraq but opted not to respond, instead supporting the Iraqi government’s efforts.In Yemen, the Houthis claimed Saudi Arabia carried out more than 100 airstrikes in Yemen over 48 hours, even as Houthis reportedly made major territorial gains along the Red Sea Coast.There were also signs of diplomatic engagement. Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan met Iranian President Dr. Masoud Pezeshkian on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS summit in New Delhi.It was the highest-level meeting between the two nations since the conflict began. The leaders underscored the importance of supporting efforts to ease tensions, promote de-escalation, and strengthen regional stability.Reports also suggest that Iran and Gulf states are expected to meet in Oman tomorrow to discuss regional issues and the Strait of Hormuz. However, it is uncertain if all countries will participate, and a concrete agreement to reopen the waterway may not be expected immediately.Meanwhile, the Houthi’s advance and the Saudi pipeline attack are adding pressure to an already disrupted regional energy and shipping network, with both the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb facing growing security concerns.

. Union Home Minister Amit Shah today said that the presence of multiple languages in India is the biggest strength of the country. Sharing a video message on Hindi Diwas today, he said that the Hindi language is not a competitive language of any other language but an important connecting thread of national unity. He said that language plays an important role in getting free of colonial mindset and stressed that replacing British laws by Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam was not only exchange of words but the reestablishment of self-pride.The Home Minister stated that under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Hindi and all the other languages are witnessing a golden period of technological development. Mr Shah highlighted that in the current time, AI tools are giving opportunities for easy translation of Indian languages.Talking about the new education policy, Mr Shah said that the policy places mother tongue at the centre of education. He highlighted that in the current scenario, studies in the streams of engineering, medical and others are taking place in multiple languages. He said that India’s culture, yoga, ayurveda and others are reaching the world through the medium of language only.The Home Minister urged the youth to learn about their mother tongue and also urged the parents to use it during conversation at their home. He also advised the citizens to not to feel ashamed while talking in their mother tongue. Mr Shah urged the citizens to resolve to make language an effective tool in the country’s journey of Viksit Bharat.

. In tennis, Kazakhstan’s Elena Rybakina defeated Belarusian Aryna Sabalenka 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 to win the US Open women’s singles final at Arthur Ashe Stadium in New York last night.This is Rybakina’s first US Open title and her third career Grand Slam championship, following her Australian Open victory earlier in the year. With the win, Rybakina officially takes over the WTA world No. 1 ranking from Sabalenka.Earlier, American Christian Harrison and Britain’s Neal Skupski clinched the men’s doubles title, defeating Germany’s Kevin Krawietz and Tim Puetz.The American-British pair won the final 6-4, 7-6 to claim their second Grand Slam title of the year, after their Australian Open victory in January.The men’s singles final will be played between Germany’s World No. 2 Alexander Zverev and local favourite Ben Shelton in New York tonight. The match is scheduled to begin at 11:30 PM Indian time.

. In Para Badminton, Tokyo Paralympic gold medallist Pramod Bhagat secured gold medal in the men’s singles SL3 category and teamed up with Sukant Kadam to win silver in the men’s doubles SL3-SU5 at the Japan International today. The six-time world champion, Bhagat produced a dominant performance in the singles final, defeating fellow Indian, Umesh Kumar 21-16, 21-8 to clinch the top honour. Bhagat then partnered Kadam in the men’s doubles SL3-SU5 category final, where the Indian pair went down 5-21, 15-21 to Indonesia’s Hikmat Ramdani and Fredy Setiawan, settling for silver. The tournament was particularly special for Kadam, who took his career medal tally to 100 over 12 years of competitive badminton.
